Those locals who were stealing from us, they were not attacked but they were stealing the cattle that we had driven down there, that we were keeping on their land, because they were taking these cattle and keeping it on their property. They were taking it to their own stables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: And those who did that were Serbs; is that right, rightly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just following on from Their Honours' questioning on those topics, cattle were certainly led away by the attackers on the 21st of June, but not your cattle. Other Serb -- other cattle belonging to Serb villagers were led away. Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you moved your cattle down to Rijeka for safekeeping, but unfortunately it didn't work out that way because the Serbs down there stole your cattle; correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So faced with that situation, you decided to move your cattle back to Bradjevina, and you did that on about the 26th. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's very clear now. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, let's turn to the 27th. On that day, your wife was not in Bradjevina, I believe.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've already said there was an attack. About what time did the attack start on that day?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: At 12.00, noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the attack started?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was about 200 metres above my house, in the field. That's also where the trench was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at the trench?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was near the trench. When the shooting started, I jumped into the trench. When I could see how many people were coming, then I pulled back from the trench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just prior to the attack starting -- I'll withdraw that. Do you know a man named Stojan Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's your cousin, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a shepherd? Or was he a shepherd, I should say.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he tending sheep or animals on that day?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: He was looking after the sheep and the goats that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the attack, did he leave the area and go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: He took the sheep and put them in the barn, and then he came home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He went to his house, did he?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he armed on the 27th [Realtime transcript read in error "17th] of June?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: He did have a rifle, but I don't know where they found him. I don't know if he was at home asleep. I don't know where they caught him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's turn to the -- your position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Brydensholt is drawing my attention to transcript 49, line 5, 17th of June, should be 27th of June; correct? MR. DI FAZIO: That is so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the 27th. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Your position, you said you were in your trench or near your trench or the trench in Bradjevina, and that was located above the hamlet of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you first notice was happening when the attack initially started? What could you see and hear?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Shooting started below the village, and then some hay started to burn and some sheds, everything that was below the village. The shooting first started below the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they haystacks and sheds associated or owned by the people who lived in the hamlet of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you first noticed shooting and you first noticed some hay starting to burn and some sheds burning. Were those haystacks or hay and the sheds belonging to inhabitants of Bradjevina, associated with --

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction when you saw the attack underway?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I went into the trench, but then when I saw that the attack had started from above and that a lot of people were coming, I had to pull back into the village. The village was already burning. Then I had to stop in a field below the house where I hid in some bushes, and I stayed there until the end of the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was that field uncultivated land?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was still above the little hamlet of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position, did you have a view across the hamlet of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, except for two houses. One was at the end of the village, and one was to the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Those two could not be seen from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that houses were burning. How many houses, would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you say, were burning?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: As soon as they were looted, they all started to burn, because a lot of soldiers entered the village. So they were entering the houses, and then as they were leaving the houses, they burnt them. The only buildings that were left were the storage areas where there was some grain or some kind of food. That was the only thing that was not set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Firstly the soldiers, were they uniformed?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably armed with guns, rifles, and automatic guns?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position in the uncultivated area of land, could you see the faces of the soldiers from time to time?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to have their names. We don't need to go into that. But did you recognise any of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of them men that you recognised from before the war, from surrounding Muslim villages, from the area, local men?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the civilians, you say that civilians accompanied the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they just men or men and women or ...

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: They were women and men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've described fires. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what you saw from your hidden position as to how -- what preceded the building being set alight or becoming ablaze. Tell the Trial Chamber what happened.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The first thing we noticed, because we had stood guard above the village, behind, we were hoping that there were three trenches behind the villages, the side facing Mocevici. We thought an attack would be coming from the woods, but the attack came from the river. They came down the river, and they blocked us from that direction. So that's where the shooting started. And they entered the village before we knew it, and whoever was caught in the village was captured. Those of us who were in the trench behind the village could escape down the flanks. So the first thing was the attack began below the village and not from above the village. That's where we expected it to come from, and that's where we were standing guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see -- tell the Trial Chamber how the buildings got -- were set on fire. What did you see?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers were entering houses, and as they were leaving, house was start to burn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see civilians going into houses?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything being taken from houses?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see being taken?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly food. Some of the lighter things, appliances, TV. No one took any TVs or freezers, the larger appliances. That was all torched along with the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say lighter things, do you mean objects, household possessions, but not food?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: When I say lighter items, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took away these items? Who actually physically carried away the lighter items and the food?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers that entered houses were taking things out, but of course they had civilians who also helped them pick things up and carry these items off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Presumably they took items out of the house when -- or dwellings and so on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, before he answers because here I think we have a bit of a confusion. Question is what did you -- I'm referring to line 22 of the previous page. What did you see being taken? Answer: "Mostly food, some of the lighter things, appliances, TV. No one took any TVs or freezer, the larger appliances. That was all torched along with the houses." So already here we have confusion as regards TVs, because they are mentioned at one point that they have been taken, at another point that they haven't. And then your question: "When you say lighter things you mean objects, household possessions but not food." The answer was: "When I say lighter items, yes," whatever that means. And then your question: "Who took away these items? Who actually physically carried away the lighter items and the food?" And so now first you excluded the food, and now you include it yourself. And then he answered: "The soldiers that entered houses were taking things out, but of course they had civilians who also helped pick things up and carry these items out." So at this stage, I honestly don't know whether TVs were taken out or not, whether they come into the -- amongst the lighter or the heavier items and whether food was actually taken, because at one stage he said food was taken, at another time you suggested that it wasn't and he seems to have agreed with you. At the moment he seems to have agreed with you. Then you suggested that it had been taken again. So I think we better clarify that a little bit. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, was food taken?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were light household possessions taken?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone taking TVs or fridges?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, in my house they -- they torched it, but they didn't take it away. It's my house I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone taking fridges or TVs from any house?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was food taken from your house and other houses in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was -- were light household possessions taken from your house and other houses in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: They took a tape recorder from my house and torched the TV, electrical heater, and -- and the freezer. And later they took the video recorder away and the refrigerator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is from your house.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you see light household possessions, I don't mean fridges, I don't mean TVs. I mean light household possessions being taken from other houses apart from your own.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was -- were cattle taken?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The cattle were driven away following the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: And they were retreating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, when you say cattle were driven away, I want a bit more detail. Do you mean they were just driven off into the fields or were they driven away and taken by the attackers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: They took it towards Mocevici from Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It might seem obvious to you, I just want to be absolutely, 100 per cent clear. Did they appear to be leading the cattle away, taking the cattle away? However you take cattle, not being experienced in that area myself.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not how it appeared. It is simply a fact they drove our cattle towards Mocevici, up in the hillside. That's the next village, the village next to ours. That's not how it appeared to us. What I mean is they did actually take it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, what about sheep? Did -- were there any sleep in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any pigs being raised in the village, the hamlet of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the fate of the pigs?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Later when I put Stojan on the cart, I saw that the pigs had been killed, but I didn't see any pigs being driven away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many pigs did you see had been slaughtered?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw three or four along the road in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want you to return to a period of time in which you were hiding in the piece of uncultivated land just above Bradjevina. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, can we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into closed session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give the Trial Chamber the names of any other persons who were killed on the 27th apart from this man Stojan? And I'm not just talking about Bradjevina. I'm talking about the area in Bradjevina and immediately around Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps I can make this quicker. Do you know someone called Ljubisa Gajic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Several quick questions for you. Was he a man who was living in the area and was he apparently killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later find his remains in 1993?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you led to his remains by a gentleman called Milutin?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a gentleman named Novica Stanojevic living in the area?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't find any remains of that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The question is, was there a man called Novica Stanojevic living in the area up until the 27th of June?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a body of Novica ever found or remains ever found or was he ever seen again?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slavko Petrovic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he disappear after the 27th of -- of June?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Vlado Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he killed during the course of the attack?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his body found?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long after the attack?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Seven or eight days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rade Jovanovic. Firstly, did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: From Stanatovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day after the 27th, the 28th obviously, did you go back to the -- to your village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see his body on that day, Rade Jovanovic, the body of Rade Jovanovic on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We picked him up and laid him down on the asphalt road at Grabovicka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Good. Thank you. On that day, the 28th of June, was Kaludra attacked as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 27th, Kaludra was torched, and on the 28th, Vranesevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting me; that was my mistake. On the 27th Kaludra was attacked?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 27th, it was torched, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Magudovici, was that attacked?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Magudovici on the 27th also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position in the uncultivated field above Bradjevina, could you see Kaludra and Magudovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not Magudovici but Kaludra, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position during the course of the attack, what was happening in Kaludra? What could you see?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Kaludra, they were just torching things because the local villagers had left the village, and they had driven their livestock away. So they just torched the village with no one in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's return to Stojan and the period of time shortly after the attack. What did you do with Stojan, the body of Stojan Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can go -- you can lead the witness in this. MR. DI FAZIO: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you put his body in a wheelbarrow and wheel them the four or five kilometres down to the main road going to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as Bratunac. From the village of Bradjevina, I wheeled him the five kilometres to the asphalt road at Grabovicka Rijeka, and that's where his son Milovan put him into a car and drove him to Basta. That's where he was buried. That's where a post-mortem was conducted. Not to Bratunac. You couldn't drive as far as Bratunac at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And on your way as you're wheeling his body down in the wheelbarrow, could you see Kaludra?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see fires burning in the dwelling houses?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, and I apologise for this, I omitted a matter, a very, very brief matter in relation to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go, go, go. MR. DI FAZIO: Can we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Closed session or private session? MR. DI FAZIO: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following day, you -- you returned to your area with -- with a group of men, I think. The 28th of June?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in company with a man called Slavko Jovanovic, I believe?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The purpose of your group was to try to recover the body of Vlado Pavlovic. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were ambushed, and I think during the course of that ambush Slavko was killed.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is during this trip back into your area of Bradjevina, did you see Ratkovici at all? Did you come close to Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We know what's happened to Bradjevina. Did you come close to Kaludra or Ducici or Dvorista?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Magudovici? Did you come close to Magudovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll leave the topic now of the 27th and the 28th. In the period of time after this attack did you stay in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: For about 20 days, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that time -- let me withdraw that. In the -- in the period of time that you stayed in Fakovici, did you see the arrival of someone called -- a man with a beard called Chetnik in company with -- nicknamed Chetnik, I should say, in company with a number of other men who you understood came from Skelani?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this man nicknamed Chetnik, with the beard, appear to be in charge of these men from Skelani?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How men was he apparently in charge of?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't give you the exact number. There was a group of men there but I couldn't give you a specific number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know you can't; I'm not asking for a specific number. But try and give us an approximation. We're talking about 2 or 3 men? Twenty?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ten or 15 men. That much is certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Were they also in possession of a truck on which was mounted some sort of anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time to get across to Serbia, what was the best way of getting across to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: By boat. There was no other way to cross. There was a bridge at Skelani, but that was the only other way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period of time that you remained in Fakovici after the 27th of June attack, could you get out to Serbia through Skelani?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that -- was there any other way apart from the river, crossing the river?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no other way, only at Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to cross the river in the period of time that you were in Fakovici? The Drina, I mean.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't, because all the boats had been pulled ashore, and they forbade everyone from crossing the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who forbade people from crossing the Drina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This group led by the man nicknamed Chetnik. They had pulled the boats ashore, and they allowed no boats to cross there around Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the man Chetnik and his group eventually leave Fakovici, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then free to cross to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that, in fact, what you did?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when Chetnik and his men left, what happened to the truck with the anti-aircraft gun? Do you know? If you don't know, say so, but if you know what its fate was, tell us.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I know that on the 5th when the attack by the Muslim forces took place on the 5th, I heard that the truck was in Fakovici, next to the house of Dragan Nikolic. I heard that he had left the truck parked just below the house. On the 5th when he came. On the 28th, when Chetnik came, the truck was brought there, but I don't know when it was returned to Fakovici again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you. Now, in between the attack on the 27th of June and your 20-day stay in Fakovici, that period of time, and the 5th of October, did you remain in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In October of 1992, did you go to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 6th. I crossed over to collect the bodies of those killed, on the 6th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it -- is it the case that you were not in Fakovici itself on the 5th when the attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the next day, the 6th, you went in and collected bodies?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you involved in that? Why did you get yourself involved in -- in collecting bodies from Fakovici? Is there any particular reason?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Serbia, on the other side of the Drina, there were many people whose relatives had -- or friends had been killed. So I had crossed over with them to help them to get their -- the bodies of those relatives and friends who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it -- what I want to know is was it a voluntary act that you did or were you ordered by someone to do this?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I volunteered to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many bodies did you locate in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: We found eight corpses at the house of the Nikolics.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone off for the Presiding Judge, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day that you were collecting bodies, did you have a chance to observe any damage in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Partly, not all of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll get you to explain that in just a moment, but firstly, you -- is it the case that you were well familiar with Fakovici? You knew the place well from before the war?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the damage that you observed on the 6th of October, you say you saw -- you saw part of it. What I want to know is this: Was -- was Fakovici only damaged in part or was it -- all of it damaged? And if you don't know the answer, tell us.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't burned down entirely. There were some buildings that had been left standing, intact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On the day that you were there collecting the bodies, did you see any Serb soldiers? VRS, I mean.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They came in trucks from Skelani, and they loaded them up. They didn't allow us to load them into boats and take them across the river, but loaded them up into the trucks and took them across via Skelani while we returned to Serbia by boat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other Serb soldiers on that day doing anything other than participating in the collection of bodies?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to show you some photos on the -- on the screen. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment. I'm drawing to a close now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Ms. Usher. If -- perhaps there could be -- you can have the benefit of both screen and the hard copy in front of you, Mr. Stevanovic. MR. DI FAZIO: And Your Honours have copies, I think. Your Honours, it's going to be my intention to tender these photographs hopefully after the witness has commented on them. Would you like me to tender them as a bundle? I think that would probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that would be preferable, Mr. Di Fazio. That's what we have done -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's what I prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- with the others. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the first photograph that you can see there. It has a number 01088083. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recognise that place?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where -- where is it located?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it may not have looked exactly the same, but when you saw it back then, when you walked into town, into the village on the 6th of October, 1992, did it -- had it suffered -- that building suffered similar damage, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was already burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Look at the next photograph, please. That photograph has a number next to it, 01088084. Do you recognise that structure?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Fakovici, right next to this one, quite close to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know whose house it is or whose place it was?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's the house of Colonel Zarko Pajkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw it back in 1992, had it suffered similar damage as depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Just look at the foreground. It's all overgrown. You see all the plants and growth all the around the house. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into Fakovici on the 6th of October, presumably that growth hadn't occurred, and apart from the damage to the house, it was a properly maintained area.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's be clear. When you went into the village on the 6th of October, was there the growth and vegetation that you can see there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't, because then it was regularly cut down and cleaned. In front -- the area in front of house then was clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Can you look at the next photograph. That's accompanied by a number, 01088085. Do you recognise that place?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Fakovici also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what it is in Fakovici, whose place it is or what building it is?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: These are the apartments of the teachers from the school in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw it on the 6th of October, 1992, did it have a roof as you can see in that photograph, or you can't recall? If you can't recall, that's fine, but if you can, let us know.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do remember, because it was right next to the road. On the 6th, it was without a roof. It had been burned. This photograph was taken later, after the roof was repaired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at the next photograph, please. That's accompanied by a number, 01088086. You recognise that structure, that building?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it damaged when you saw it on the 6th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any idea whose place that is?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the house of the Drago Zikic who was captured in Srebrenica. He was a postman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at the next photo. That's accompanied by the number 01088087. Do you recognise that place?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose place is it, if you know?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This was the house owned by the forestry company. This is where the forest warden or the forest keeper lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw it on the 6th of October, 1992, had it suffered similar damage?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not apparent from this photograph in particular, but can you say when you saw it on the 6th of October, 1992, that it appeared to have suffered fire damage?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next photo, please. This photo here is accompanied by the number 01088088. Do you recognise that structure and is it in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the old school in Fakovici. It was burned down on the 6th, but now it has been re-roofed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you -- okay. So it didn't have a roof when you saw it that day when you walked into the village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again. Had it appeared to have suffered fire damage?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And look at this next photograph numbered 01088089. Can you help us with this -- this structure or not?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This was the weekend house of a person called Bozic who lived in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I ask the witness how come he can recognise it from -- from what he can see here in the photo? What's so distinctive about it that makes you recognise it without the least doubt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went to school in Fakovici. See, that's where I went to school, and I completed fifth grade in this school. So I know Fakovici as well as I know my own village. I know the inhabitants there, the houses, where people live, and I know all the buildings along the road. This building is right behind the school or right next to the school. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm glad that Your Honour clarified that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photo, please. That's accompanied by the number 01088098. Sorry, let me repeat that. I've made a mistake. 090.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Last three digits are 090. MR. DI FAZIO: That's correct. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose place is that surrounded by the flowers there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember this house exactly. I cannot remember if it's the house of the Markovics or someone else's. There was a house like this behind the old school, right behind the old school, but I don't know exactly what it is. I do know that it had burned down completely and there were several houses around there that had burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Please feel free to express any uncertainty. Can you say that -- even though you don't know whose house it is, can you say that it was -- that it's in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this house is situated in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. This photograph that I show you, the last one, 01088091, do you recognise this area at all? It appears to be a wall.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This has been demolished completely, so it's very hard to tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Well, I won't ask you any further questions about that.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you're tendering this bundle of photos in evidence? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I do, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And they are being admitted in evidence together as one document, and that will be Prosecution Exhibit P405. Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you said earlier that you lived in Bradjevina for most of your life. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Right until the war I lived in Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the attacks that you have described to the Court today, were you ever able to go back to your farm and land?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can go as a tourist to see it, but I could not live there. Everything has been destroyed. There's no electricity. There's no road. Everything has been grown over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of your former neighbours who used to live with you in Bradjevina ever go back and live there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No one has returned out of the whole local community. The whole local community is empty. Nobody has gone back to live there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place is now overgrown with weeds and remain in that state?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Now, it's obvious that we are not going to finish with the cross-examination today. I mean, I take it you won't finish in 45 plus ten -- 55 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I will not be able to finish the cross-examination, and I would appreciate it very much if we could make a break now, and then I could complete one topic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The other things that arise out of -- out of all this. It basically means that we are moving this witness to Monday, which brings me to this: The next witness that we had for Monday, I don't think he has any protective measures, but anyway, witness number 6 who was scheduled to come here on the 1st of November to testify on exactly the same events as this witness, you had indicated that you required three hours for that witness. For this particular witness you had indicated two hours, for the other one, three hours. I have browsed through his statement, and I don't know. I mean, I -- more or less we are in the same -- in the same situation. But if you require three hours, as you did for this particular witness, for the next one, then basically I don't think it's the case of bringing over to The Hague the other witness, number 7, the woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the first thing I wanted to draw your attention to, because if you need -- we need on Monday, we need to finish this witness, and then you need three hours for the next witness, and I -- I presume they need another two hours at least for the same witness. So basically that would cover Monday and Tuesday. So there's no point in bringing number 7 as well. There's no point in bringing number 7 unless --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can check during the break if we can limit number 6 instead of three hours to two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but still. I mean, what are you going to solve?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And number 7 as well to two hours. Does that make any difference in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, one can work it out because it's just basic arithmetic. We have three hours, 45 minutes every sitting, so that's -- you have seven hours and a half, seven hours and a half. We -- I reckon that we need next 45 minutes plus another hour and a half for this one, so that's an hour and a half from seven hours and a half, leaves you with six hours. If you are prepared to divide the six hours, three hours each for each witness, one and a half hour you, and one hour and a half for the Defence, yes, we can go along. But if you require more than one and a half hours each we can't make it. That's the first point I wanted to make. The second --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We need more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The second point is this -- I think so because I have got the statements here. The second point is this: We mentioned earlier on -- or we have agreed basically that Mr. Gow will not come here on -- starting on the 29th but will come here starting on the 22nd. If I recall well, we -- you had indicated then the days of the 23rd, 24th, to 25th for the video-conferencing in case we accept that -- that motion. So assuming for the time being the likelihood that we accept that motion and that we grant it for the video-conferencing, you have to think about moving those dates, and I know that you require for that purpose at least three weeks to four weeks to do that. So in the break, during the break think about these things and tell us whether you are dropping number 7 for the time being from next week's list and whether you would move the video-conferencing from those days to some other day, in which case please communicate the days to us so that if we grant the motion and need to draw the -- up the decision, we will indicate the new dates and not the dates which would require you to then file another motion or note to change the dates and so on and so forth. So I'm just asking you to address these problems. All right? On a management, housekeeping business. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to ask the Prosecutor to keep in mind that the cross-examination of witness number 7, who is very important to us, we would need at least two hours as well as for this next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I would think so, because they are more or less testifying on -- on the same events. And -- anyway, I said I browsed through the other two statements as I could. Browsed, literally browsed, and I don't think we can finish either of them in an hour and a half on either side to be honest with you. But it's up to you. If you can agree on that, let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will get back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So we will have a 25-minute break, which basically means that we start at ten to one, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. Oh, I see Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to update you regarding scheduling. We did some exercising, and I have some final draft before me, but anyhow, we will provide you with a schedule, a new schedule, in hard copy on Monday first thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The important thing is that you have taken into consideration that I said earlier. The rest is up to you. I mean, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. We have taken it into consideration, and it will mean that we plan Professor Gow, then, in this first week after the break in November, starting the 22nd, 23rd, 24th, and then we have two projected videolink witnesses pending on motion and to be decided by Trial Chamber. That will end that week, the 25th and the 26th. Then we will slot in the Tuesday witness and then everything goes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect. Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic. Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will remind you that in 2000, you gave a statement to the OTP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed that statement?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement, when speaking about Mocevici, which you again referred to today, you stated that in April or in May 1992, you were in Mocevici and that you saw Muslims putting up barricades that were meant to prevent the movement of any tanks or heavy weaponry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those you meant were Serb tanks or artillery; right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whose. In Lipova woods, there were wooden beams across the road with several metres between them. They were afraid that tanks would come from Srebrenica, because Srebrenica at the time, there were Serbs there, and those people were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. That means, doesn't it -- doesn't this indicate that the Muslims felt threatened at the time?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, otherwise they would not have been putting up barricades had they not felt threatened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification. You said that you knew a man named Slavko Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slavko Jovanovic was a member of the Main Board of the SDS for Bratunac municipality. Is that not correct? You can continue, sir.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, we were in Fakovici towards Skelani municipality. We had nothing to do with Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not correct that Mr. Slavko Jovanovic was president of the Fakovici SDS local branch?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that Mr. Slavko Jovanovic was in charge of obtaining weapons for the Fakovici area?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was in charge or not. As far as I know, he was the one who procured weapons. Whether he was officially in charge, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. The Fakovici area includes your own village and the surrounding hamlets, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you closely cooperated with Slavko Jovanovic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were actively involved in obtaining weapons for the Serbian population of the village of Ratkovici, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, because you had distributed weapons to the population, you clashed with some of the local Serbs; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, while you were distributing weapons to the Serb population of the entire area, there was coordination with the JNA and certain people from Serbia. Are you perhaps aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean this is not true?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It may as well be true, it's just that I'm not aware of it, and I did not do any coordination. Whether perhaps Slavko was involved or anyone else may have been in charge, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that anyone at all was maintaining contact, I mean the people in Fakovici or in your own village, with people from the JNA and certain other individuals from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I have no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that the Fakovici area received weapons from Serbia by raft or by boat across the River Drina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It may as well have been the case, but I don't know. We were up in the hills. As I said before during the examination-in-chief, we had driven our cattle away, and they stole our cattle down in the area near the river. We were more reliant on the hilly area over there. We were Srebrenica, and they were Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you can't rule out such a possibility, can you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't rule it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today in your testimony, you referred to the village of Ruljevici.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a part of Ratkovici -- or, rather, of their hamlet of Vranesevici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Vranesevici belongs to Bratunac, and Ratkovici belongs to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not correct that this is very near your own village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the exact distance between Ruljevici and your own village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Ruljevici and your own village are actually on the same side of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, on the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's true. Isn't it true that in Ruljevici there was the main training camp for Serb soldiers as well as the storage facilities for weapons even prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, Mr. Stevanovic, that in the surroundings of this camp in Ruljevici, which was near where you lived, prior to the outbreak of war there had been mounting tensions between the ethnic groups, and there was a scandal over the storage facility where weapons were being kept on account of which high municipal delegations came to Ruljevici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that because I was not a member of the SDS. Therefore, I was not involved in any of those negotiations, neither those regarding weapons nor the other things. I was just an ordinary farmer. Whether there was anything like that that actually happened or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please be given one of the maps that were tendered this morning, preferably P402 and please locate on this map the location of the village of Ruljevici, Ruljevici, please, because it's not immediately visible here, or apparent. I don't know. If you don't see it, sir, could you just at least indicate on the map the approximate location as you think it is in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no writing saying Ruljevici here, but it might be this hamlet marked right here. Just close to Vranesevici.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, close to Vranesevici, down towards the Drina, where it says Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the witness to point Vranesevici out on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, Mr. Stevanovic, was: Isn't it true -- Your Honours, my apologies. I did not notice that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question to you was not whether you were personally involved in that. Rather, my question was: Is it not true that a scandal broke out over that storage facility, Serbs' storage facility where weapons were being kept prior to the war, and because of this a high municipal delegation arrived in the town?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no scandal whatsoever, at least to the extent that I was familiar with that particular situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard nothing about the president of Srebrenica municipality and his deputy alongside with the most responsible people in Srebrenica, actually came there to look into the warehouse situation?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't even know who the president of Srebrenica was at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The president of municipality doesn't exactly come to your village every day. It's not an everyday occurrence, is it no?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. By no means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. I'll move on to ask you about something else now. The Serb population of your own village and the other villages in the Fakovici area, even prior to the outbreak of war they caused unrest among the Muslims in the area by shooting; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. This was certainly not the case with my village. My own hamlet of Bradjevina, certainly not. As for the other villages, Fakovici --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ratkovici, for example?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ratkovici, I certainly would have heard sounds of shooting had that been the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're trying to say is that you never heard sounds of shooting at night coming from those villages, nor did anyone publicly speak about that at any time.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was shooting from Mocevici and from Ratkovici on several occasions, not just once, in 1992, because in 1992, I gave a statement that he had been killed on the 26th of May, and there had been shooting prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was in relation to events prior to the outbreak of war. Did you ever hear or did anyone publicly speak about the local population of Ratkovici and the surroundings shooting at night, causing -- firing at night, causing unrest among the local Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard no such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Muslim village of Poznanovici is in the immediate vicinity of your own village, Bradjevina which is a hamlet in Ratkovici, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's just the other side of the hill. Ratkovici is closer to Poznanovici than my village. You can have a look at the map to see for yourself if you like.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness a map, the map that we have used before. The map is from the Zvornik file, the Zvornik folder. I think it's a bit more accurate, this map, because it contains all of these hamlets with the corresponding markings. We shall not use the map now as an exhibit, but we would like to have it distributed to all the parties, including the Chamber. We would like the witness to point out a number of different villages on this map right here. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I have no problem with the exercise Madam Vidovic is conducting. I only express some concerns about this process of showing material to witnesses that is not identified -- either marked for identification or tendered. At some point later in the transcript should it ever becomes necessary that we need to go back months and months down the track and you try to understand this evidence, then we'll have to have something that's marked for identification or an exhibit. So I've got no problem, but let's have it marked at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the suggestion or the remark of Mr. Di Fazio makes a hell of a lot of sense. I suggest that you tender it. There's no problem in admitting it, and we can always use it as a reference if we need to relation to the testimony of this witness. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honours. We can do that. However, we expected that during their examination-in-chief, the OTP would use maps that both parties could then find helpful. However, we would like to request that this map be marked at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, could you please have a look here --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be D46.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is being admitted as Defence Exhibit D46.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please show the Chamber the village of Ratkovici on this map that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could use a pen to point it out.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's marked already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, but could you please point it out again for us. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Give him the pointer, please. Can you just -- yes. For the record, the Trial Chamber affirms that the witness has pointed to a place called Ratkovici, marked Ratkovici on the map D46. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please now point to the Mlecva area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness points to an area which is marked Mlecva on the map D46. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you now shown us the Brezani area.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And for the record, the witness points to a place named -- named Brezani on the map D46.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, Witness, can you please again show us the Fakovici area? It's marked next to Vranesevici. It's off the map a little. Can you just confirm whether it's the same general direction? If you could look at Vranesevici.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Grabovicka Rijeka, Vranesevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Vranesevici. And just next to it says Fakovici, three kilometres; is that correct? If you can have a look, please. It can be seen clearly, but you're pointing the right way. Thank you, thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to the words "Fakovici" to the right of Vranesevici on the map between line 86 and 84.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please show Poznanovici, the village of Poznanovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness points to a spot on the map indicated with the name Poznanovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, Witness, I would like you to indicate Potkorjen. Is it not true that Dedici is nearby except but it's not marked?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to Potkorjen on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Witness, can you please indicate the village of Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness, for the record, points to a place indicated with the name Mocevici on map D46.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the village of Orlica. Is it not true that there is a village called Orlica nearby?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are two Orlicas. One is supposedly Gornji Orlica --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gornja and Donje. Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both. I want both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record, the witness indicates both Donja Orlica and Gornja Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can I just ask you some questions in relation to these, please. Is it not true that the villages of Poznanovici, Potkorjen, and Dedici are Muslim villages and hamlets?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were telling us about the abandoned villages where no one had returned, you mentioned your Bradjevina. I will ask you to show where it is later. You mentioned Bradjevina, but isn't it also true that you mentioned these three villages, Poznanovici, Potkorjen, and Dedici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are Muslim villages which had overgrown and to which no one had returned?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify that. Could you also indicate now your Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not on the map, so I will show you that approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you can just indicate that with an X, please.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put that X in a circle, please, and put your initials next to it. So for the record, the witness put an X indicating the village of Bradjevina and fixed his initials next to it. The spot indicated by him is below Grabovica on map D46, and to the left of Vranesevici. Let's proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Stevanovic, that Poznanovici, Potkorjen and Dedici are surrounded -- which are Muslim village, Poznanovici, Potkorjen, and Dedici, that they are Muslim villages and they are surrounded by Serb villages of Brezani, Ratkovici, Mlecva and Fakovici over there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. From Mlecva and Ratkovici, but from Brezani, Osmace are much closer to Potkorjen, Dedici than Brezani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you immediately indicate Osmace on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want him to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, I want him to mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you mark it with an O and then put that O in a circle, please. And put your initials next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like you to pay attention to the villages which we discussed before. These are Zapolje, Orlica, and Mocevici. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Orlica is half and half. There is a Serbian Orlica and there is a Roma Orlica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These Romas, are they of the Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what their religious affiliation is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they perhaps expelled in April and May 1992 of any ethnic -- of any ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In May, they were expelled just as we were. They were expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who expelled them?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: How should I know who expelled them? I don't know if they were expelled by the TO from Bratunac or Skelani. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These Territorial Defences that you mentioned, this is the Serbian Territorial Defence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course they were not expelled by Muslims. Mocevici could not expel Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I wanted to ask you something else now. Is it true that the population of Poznanovici, which you just indicated, even before the war protested, frequently protested because Serbs from the area of Ratkovici and Fakovici fired in the direction of their village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now I would like to ask you to look at your Ratkovici. You indicated that.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Bradjevina is mine, not Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The hamlet of Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The local commune was Ratkovici. The hamlet was Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you agree that in 1991, Ratkovici was a large village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't really a large village. I have it in a statement how many households there were in that village. It wasn't a large village by population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ratkovici did not have more than 30 households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put an excerpt from the population census, the census of population households, property, from 1990 which was issued in Sarajevo in May 1991. This is the last official population census of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Could the witness please be shown that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on page 3 could you look at the information for Ratkovici. For Ratkovici. It states here that Ratkovici had 338 inhabitants, 85 households, 111 apartments, and 77 agricultural farms or properties. Could you lease look at this excerpt?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that Ratkovici had 85 households, 111 apartments, and 77 farms?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's true, but including the villages around the -- Ratkovici. This talks about the entire local community of Ratkovici and only Ratkovici is mentioned. The other local communities are not mentioned. This is a total number of the population.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the names of the hamlets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told the Prosecutor that in 2000, today you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreters -- the interpreters did not manage to catch the final part of the witness's reply, answer. I took it that he was mentioning names of villages which he considers to form part of Ratkovici commune. If he could -- if he could -- if he could finish his reply and then we have a question from Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you understand to be the village of Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: All the hamlets in that local community. There are no Magudovici, Bradjevina, Dvorista, Ducici, Polimci, Kaludra. There is no information about those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
