utterances.text: I must say I'm still lit bit confused. Now you speak of Ratkovici and it seems to have two different meanings. Ratkovici as own village, and around Ratkovici is a commune which comprises other hamlets. Now, when you spoke about, I think, 30 or something households of Ratkovici, did you speak of the village of Ratkovici not including the hamlets around Ratkovici? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, only the Gornji and Donji Ratkovici. They have about 30 houses. And then it's plus these other hamlets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So the number we have here on this exhibit would include beside Gornji Ratkovici all of the other hamlets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Go ahead, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question would be: Could you please tell us, which are those hamlets which would be a part of the Ratkovici local commune?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Donji Ratkovici and Gornji Ratkovici, Dvorista, Ducici, Magudovici, Bradjevina, Kaludra, Koljanica [phoen], Poznanovici, Dedici, and Potkorjen were all part of the Ratkovici local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. I would like you to stay on the same page and look a little bit higher on the page when all the villages are mentioned. You will see the village of Poznanovici with all the information which is completely different. Look at it. Poznanovici, 444 inhabitants, 68 households, 76 apartments, 66 farms. What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am talking about the information about Dedici, Potkorjen, and Poznanovici, because when the census was carried out they were separated, this is what I know. Because here, there is no Potkorjen and Dedici. There's only Poznanovici here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just said here that Poznanovici was a hamlet, which was a part of Ratkovici and that those households should have been included in this number that you read out. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right. They should have been included, but they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will continue with my questions. I would just like to have this exhibit -- have a number, have -- be given a Defence Exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is being admitted as Defence Exhibit D47. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to ask the usher -- I cannot see the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The ELMO -- the ELMO is constructing the view of the witness to counsel. So if you could. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something else, Mr. Stevanovic. Mr. Stevanovic, you were a close friend of General Milenko Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps who visited you often, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that you even received an M-72 machine-gun which you had with you throughout the whole war?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. That is a lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said today that you bought your weapon.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something about the attack itself on Ratkovici on the 21st of June. You said today that you were in Bradjevina during the attack. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that Bradjevina is a few kilometres from Ratkovici. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Three kilometres as the crow flies, I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe that's not the exact measurement. It could be less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me that -- are you actually saying you're between Ratkovici and Bradjevina and the nearby area that there is a valley?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a hilly region, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Grabovacka river, the small river, flows in between those villages.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a hilly area?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that on the 21st of June, 1992, it was foggy that morning.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to see, then, uniforms and weapons at a distance of two to three kilometres in this region? It's true that you were not able to see that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not correct, because when Ratkovici was set on fire and when they had gone out into the fields to burn the agricultural buildings from the other side --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it means that it is correct that you did not see who torched those buildings.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw who torched them, but I did not recognise by face who it was of those people, but I could see that this was done by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that you saw this in this hilly area from a distance of two to three kilometres?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to say is that Bradjevina and Polimci and Gornji Ratkovici look to each other while Donji Ratkovici and Ducici are behind the hill and you cannot see them from Bradjevina so you cannot see them at all although they are all next to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that when we go there and when we stand at that same place we will be able to see what you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are saying that you could see people moving in that terrain?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is correct that you did not have binoculars? You said that.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to remind you of your testimony to the Prosecutor in 2000. You said then I -- I would just draw your attention if you would need it I would like to provide you with that statement. It is page 4 of the Bosnian version. You said that you heard women and men there banging on their pots and pans in order to make a noise?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that for us? I would like to ask you to explain to us what was happening.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The shouting, the noise, the swearing, yes, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, weren't these desperate people who had to bang on their pots and pans in order to frighten the enemy women and civilians who were risking their lives in this way in order to get to food? Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Madam from the Defence, I don't know whether they were forced to do that because they were attacking us. So that means they were not defending themselves. They were going to burn and loot Serbian villages. Whether they were expelled or not, that is something that I don't know, but it is for sure that in places where they were surrounded by Serbian villages, they were probably expelled. But I'm just talking about what I know and not what I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know about them banging their pots on that day?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now something that you have referred to already. Is it not true that the Serb army, including fighters from your own village, held under siege several thousands of peoples -- of people who had been expelled from the surrounding Muslim villages in the woods in the areas of Poznanovici and Mocevici villages? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I object to that question. There's no specification of when or how or why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I was going to ask when. When, how or why it's a different matter, but what time frame are you referring to, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to rephrase my question, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not correct, Witness, that the Serb army, between April and -- between April of 1992 and late 1992 and especially in May and July 1992, held under siege several thousands of persons who had been expelled from the surrounding Muslim villages in the woods in the area of those Muslim villages that we referred to?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, then, is true? Awhile ago you said that you knew they had been expelled.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Who could have laid siege to Poznanovici at that time if everyone was just defending their own houses, the population in the Fakovici area? There wasn't a single unit to be found in Fakovici in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that. We'll get to that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you are concluding on this event, go ahead. If you're moving to something new, I think we better adjourn. It's up to you. You've got one, two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just another question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please, is it not true that people from those villages were expelled in April, May, and June 1992 and that they were staying in the surrounding woods? Did you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: How could I have been aware of how many people were in the woods or were in Poznanovici and Mocevici and who had withdrawn from their villages?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is true that they left their village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, they certainly withdrew from their village, but I didn't go to these villages to see for myself whether they were still there or they had left. I didn't go to any village, Muslim or Serb. I was in Bradjevina where I lived until the fall of Bradjevina. After that, I spent 20 days in Fakovici, perhaps give or take a day or two, and then I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will stop right here and continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stevanovic that brings your testimony to an end for today. I was very optimistic in the beginning of the sitting that you would have gone home for the weekend. Unfortunately, that is not possible. You need to stay here, and I'm sure we'll finish off with you on Monday when we reconvene. I thank everyone, and have a nice weekend, and we will all meet again on Monday. Please check which courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
